text: You open a new website, ready to explore. All you want is a seamless experience, a quick digital journey.
But before you can begin, a huge banner slides up. “Accept Cookies?” it demands, blocking your view. This mandatory roadblock is on every site.
You might assume this protects *your* privacy, giving *you* control. You look for a “no” button, but it's often hidden, making you wonder.
Regulations made companies *responsible* for asking. But instead of user-friendly choices, they shifted the burden to *you*. It's easier to make you click.
What's the cost? Not your choice, but their compliance. You trade seconds for a performance, a forced interaction that rarely empowers.
Next time, you'll still click. Now you understand it's not a genuine dialogue. It’s an invisible system, a theatrical hurdle in your digital day.
